question: Does the 1995 NAST Transactions abstract document source-reported fish research in the Malabon-Tullahan system, and how precisely can that evidence be localized?

source.title: Histoarchitecture of the intestines of wild and laboratory acclimated mosquito fish, Gambusia affinis affinis, from the Malabon River
source.citation: Delfin, R., & Herrera, A. A. (1995). Histoarchitecture of the intestines of wild and laboratory acclimated mosquito fish, Gambusia affinis affinis, from the Malabon River. NAST Transactions, Volume 17, Biological Sciences, p. 251.
source.accessMethod: Reviewed the public NAST/DOST-hosted PDF text for the Biological Sciences section, pp. 250-251. The page is a short research abstract, not a full methods/results paper. No restriction was bypassed and no local copy, figure, or table was retained.
source.reuse: No item-specific open license or reuse terms were identified in the reviewed PDF. This review records minimal bibliographic and research-scope facts only; publication approval is false.

studyScope.fieldEvidence: The abstract states that anterior intestines of wild Gambusia affinis affinis from three tributaries of the Malabon-Tullahan River were compared with fish acclimated in a laboratory for 30 days. It also mentions a comparison between fish from the Malabon River and fish in the College of Science pond at UP Diliman.
studyScope.studyPurpose: Comparative intestinal histoarchitecture under wild and laboratory-acclimated conditions; the abstract is not presented as a fish-community inventory or abundance survey.
samplingDetailsNotReported: number of wild or laboratory fish
studyScope.localityDecision: Retain only at the source-described Malabon-Tullahan system level. Do not assign the samples to a named tributary, specific NCR city, mapped site, or coordinate.

identityAndReuse.nameDecision: Preserve Gambusia affinis affinis as the source-reported label. No independent specimen identification or taxonomic crosswalk was performed; the PDF text extraction contains OCR noise around the binomial.
identityAndReuse.copyrightDecision: No item-specific reuse terms were identified in the reviewed PDF. Do not reproduce its abstract, images, or underlying data; any app publication needs separate rights and evidence review.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain this as a historical research lead documenting a source-reported wild-fish sample from three unnamed Malabon-Tullahan tributaries; it is not a georeferenced occurrence or a representative river inventory.

nonClaims: The abstract does not name the three tributaries or give dates, methods, effort, specimen counts, or voucher identifiers.
The source's proliferation statement is historical author interpretation, not a current population assessment or independent invasive-status determination.
A Malabon-Tullahan system-level label does not identify a specific reach or establish a sample in every city crossed by the river system.
No current fish presence, abundance, catchability, fishing access, legal harvest, water safety, or species-diet guidance is established.
nextActions: Keep this source research-only unless an authorized, more detailed primary report supplies dates, tributary names, methods, sample identifiers, and reuse terms.
Continue the NCR waterbody inventory and separate freshwater, brackish, and Manila Bay evidence; this abstract does not complete any of those coverage lanes.
